A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain the complete main paper and Appendices A–H. Text, equations, algorithms, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original bandit simulations using MovieLens 25M and Goodreads in Section 4, with additional synthetic experiments and an asymmetric-PE comparison in Appendices A and C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices A and C, including the dataset-derived simulations and synthetic experiments.

M1.justification: PE, PE-CS, asymmetric-PE, and FT-UCB retain the same procedures, inputs, and components. Replacing 'optimal arm' with 'best reward arm' clarifies the existing algorithm description without changing its operation.

E1.justification: Both versions use MovieLens 25M and Goodreads genre-based bandit simulations and the same synthetic four-arm instances. No dataset, task, or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the UCB-CS Known ℓ comparator for PE. Figure 2 and the appendix toy experiment retain ETC-CS, UCB-CS, and TS-CS for PE-CS; the omission of UCB-CS from Figure 2's time-series panels is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same rating normalization, randomly assigned costs, regret metrics, reference-arm and subsidy sweeps, and terminal horizon T = 5 million. The synthetic experiment parameters in Appendices A and C also match.

E4.justification: The cost-versus-quality tradeoff plots in Figures 5–6, linear-regret example in Figure 7, toy-instance sensitivity study in Figure 8, and asymmetric-PE comparison in Figure 9 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 1 still reports 25 independent runs per algorithm, Figure 2 reports 50, and Appendix A's toy experiment reports 50 runs per instance. Repeated-run and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The plotted results in Figures 1–2 and 5–9 and the instance values in Figures 3–4 match across versions. The reported rankings, regret trends, and qualitative findings in Section 4 and Appendices A and C are retained.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1–3.4 and the definitions, bounds, derivations, and proofs in Appendices D–H are unchanged. The revised arm terminology and reference-arm indexing sentence restate the existing setup rather than introduce new mathematical assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.2 retain the same problem extensions, logarithmic regret guarantees, PE optimality claim, and qualified PE-CS optimality and empirical claims. No core contribution is added, removed, or strengthened.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of sample reuse, baseline unreliability, and performance versus reliability. The discussion of why PE-CS is not order-optimal for all instances in Section 3.2 and Appendix E is unchanged.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, data-construction instructions, synthetic-instance parameters, and code-access footnote are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same ETC-CS exploration-budget specification and chosen constant c = 5.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to Sinha et al. (2021), Improved-UCB, and constrained-bandit research are unchanged. Section 2's wording corrections do not revise the relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized copyedits, including 'conversation rate' to 'conversion rate' in Section 1.1, 'optimal arm' to 'best reward arm' in Sections 2–3, and grammar and spelling corrections in Section 4. Appendix G's heading changes from 'Full Cost-Subsidy Setting' to 'Subsidized Best Reward Setting'; the document structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, Tables 1–2, and the algorithm displays retain their designs, captions, structure, and placement. No figure or table is added, removed, redrawn, or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 improves terminological precision by distinguishing the best-reward arm from the cheapest feasible optimal arm in Sections 2–3, aligns Appendix G's heading with the main terminology, and corrects several language errors. These are limited clarity improvements; the methods, theoretical support, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
